high.title: Exported component consumes attacker-controlled Intent data
high.description:
Two findings in this app combine into a single exploitable path: "Implicit component export due to targetSdkVersion" and "Arbitrary fragment instantiation in MainActivity via 'fname' Intent".

Attack path:
1. Attacker sends crafted Intent to MainActivity (AndroidManifest.xml)
2. MainActivity receives Intent extra 'fname' (MainActivity.java)
3. 'fname' is passed to Util.getFragmentInstance (MainActivity.java)
4. isValidFragment performs insufficient blacklist check (MainActivity.java)
5. Target fragment is dynamically instantiated and loaded (MainActivity.java)
high.impact: The component is invokable by any app on the device and acts on the Intent it is handed without validating it, so a malicious app drives the target app's privileged behaviour with data of its choosing.
high.recommendation: Guard the component with a signature-level permission, or unexport it. Validate every Intent extra before use, and never forward a nested Intent received from a caller.

medium.title: Arbitrary fragment instantiation in MainActivity via 'fname' Intent
medium.description: The MainActivity is exported (as the launcher activity) and reads a string 'fname' from an Intent extra. This value is used as an argument to Util.getFragmentInstance(fname) to dynamically instantiate and load a fragment. The validation check in isValidFragment() only blacklists class names containing '.EmailFragment', allowing an attacker to specify any other fragment class in the application to be loaded by providing a crafted Intent extra. This can lead to unauthorized access to internal app screens or the execution of privileged actions associated with other fragments.

if (fname != null && !fname.equals("") && edu.ksu.cs.benign.MainActivity.this.isValidFragment(fname).booleanValue()) {
android.support.v4.app.FragmentTransaction ft = edu.ksu.cs.benign.MainActivity.this.getSupportFragmentManager().beginTransaction();
ft.replace(edu.ksu.cs.benign.R.id.my_placeholder, edu.ksu.cs.benign.Util.getFragmentInstance(fname));

info.title: Implicit component export due to targetSdkVersion
info.description: The app targets API level 27, allowing components with intent-filters (like MainActivity) to be exported implicitly.
info.impact: While MainActivity is intended to be reachable as the launcher, implicit export can lead to unintended exposure of other components in larger apps.
info.recommendation: Update targetSdkVersion to 31 or higher and explicitly set android:exported for all components.

reasons: Implicit export is a prerequisite that only becomes a vulnerability if an internal component is exposed. Kept at Informational: the CVSS vector, scored for an attacker with local access and high privileges, still gives Low.
warnings: Implicit export only applies below targetSdk 31; confirm the app's targetSdkVersion before treating this as exploitable.

info.title: No network security config declared
info.description: The app declares neither android:networkSecurityConfig nor usesCleartextTraffic, so it relies on platform defaults and pins no domain. With targetSdkVersion 27 those defaults still permit cleartext HTTP (see the cleartext finding).
info.impact: Without pinning, anyone who gets a CA trusted on the device can read and alter the app's TLS traffic.
info.recommendation: Declare a network security config that disables cleartext and pins the domains that carry sensitive traffic.

reasons: No certificate pinning. Pinning defends against an attacker who already controls a trusted CA or the device's trust store. Without one of those, TLS is still doing its job. It becomes a finding when paired with what the unpinned channel actually carries.
Lack of pinning is a prerequisite that only becomes a vulnerability if a sensitive channel is intercepted.

info.title: targetSdkVersion 27 permits cleartext traffic by default
info.description: targetSdk 27 predates API 28, where cleartext HTTP became opt-in. The app targets Android API level 27, which permits cleartext (HTTP) traffic by default.
info.impact: Sensitive data transmitted over HTTP can be intercepted or modified by a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacker.

reasons: Cleartext permitted by configuration. The flag permits HTTP; it does not show that anything is sent over it. Name a request that actually goes out in cleartext, and what it carries, and this is a genuine finding.
Cleartext permission is a prerequisite that only becomes a vulnerability if a sensitive request is actually sent over HTTP.
warnings: Cleartext is blocked by default from targetSdk 28; confirm the declared target and any network security config.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 22 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "edu.ksu.cs.benign". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task. The app targets API level 27 and does not specify an empty taskAffinity, making it susceptible to task hijacking on Android 10 and lower.
info.impact: A malicious app with the same taskAffinity can position its own activities on top of the victim app's activity, potentially phishing for user credentials.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.
